answer: Persistent work-ledger gating.** Each identity accumulates a verified activity record; new identities start at zero credit and cannot transact above a small cap until they pass it. Honest agents wander slowly up the ledger through real work, while an attacker must run every clone through the same costly ramp before it can do damage. Clones that stall near the inlet of the ledger stay capped and useless. A shared haven of trusted records means honest history can't be cheaply copied onto fakes. Cost: full duplicate effort per clone.
